Solution

Financial Crime Operations

Financial crime operations generate some of the highest-stakes work in regulated firms. Alerts arrive in volume, cases move between teams, and every decision has to be explainable to a supervisor. We design the workflows that connect screening, investigation, decisioning and reporting, so that analysts spend their time on judgement and the record builds itself.

Capabilities

From onboarding to SAR, controlled end to end

We design the workflows across the financial crime lifecycle, using the screening and monitoring engines you already run as inputs to controlled operations.

Anti-money laundering (AML)

Alert generation, triage and disposition workflows, with thresholds, tuning evidence and quality assurance sampling built into the process.

Know your customer (KYC)

Structured document collection, identity verification steps and refresh cycles, with a record of what was checked, by whom and against which standard.

Customer due diligence (CDD)

Risk-rated onboarding journeys that route cases to the right depth of review and capture beneficial ownership and source of funds consistently.

Enhanced due diligence (EDD)

Escalation paths for high-risk relationships, with defined evidence requirements, senior approval and documented rationale for each decision.

Case management

A single case record for alerts and investigations, with stages, service levels, ownership, linked evidence and an activity log that cannot be edited after the fact.

Investigations

Tasking, hypothesis tracking and findings capture for complex investigations, with access restricted to people with a need to know.

Screening

Sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening workflows, including potential-match review queues, dispositions and rescreening schedules.

Workflow orchestration

Coordinated movement of work across screening, KYC, case and reporting tools, with routing rules that are versioned and reviewable.

Evidence management

Evidence linked to decisions at the point of decision, with retention rules, version control and retrieval that works under examination pressure.

SAR processes

Suspicious activity reporting workflows with restricted access, tipping-off controls, MLRO review gates and a complete record of filing decisions.

Reference workflow

Every stage has an owner, a clock and a record

Each stage has a named owner, a service level, defined inputs and a mandatory record. Work cannot move forward without the evidence the next stage requires.

Typical challenges

Where financial crime operations come under pressure

  • Alert volumes that outpace analyst capacity, creating backlogs and prioritisation by intuition
  • Investigation notes spread across email, documents and case tools, making the decision trail hard to reconstruct
  • Quality assurance that samples after the fact, rather than controlling the process as it runs
  • Model and rule changes made without a documented approval route or back-testing evidence
  • Restricted SAR information leaking into general case channels, creating tipping-off risk

Expected outcomes

What a controlled financial crime operation looks like

Shorter time from alert to disposition, with service levels that are measured rather than estimated

Consistent decision records that can be produced for a supervisory request within hours

Quality assurance built into the workflow, with defect rates visible to team leads

A controlled change process for rules, thresholds and routing logic

Questions

Financial crime operations: common questions

Do you replace our screening or transaction monitoring system?

No. We design the workflows around the systems you already run and connect them with controlled integrations. Core monitoring engines remain systems of record, and our work sits in the operational layer where cases, evidence and decisions are managed.

Can AI be used in investigations?

Yes, within defined boundaries. Typical uses are drafting case summaries, extracting information from documents and surfacing relevant adverse media for review. The analyst remains accountable for the disposition, and every AI output is logged with its reviewer.

How do you handle SAR confidentiality?

SAR workflows are designed with restricted visibility, separate evidence stores where required, and gating controls that prevent the subject of a report being notified through routine case communications. Design choices are reviewed with your MLRO before build.

How long does a typical engagement take?

A focused workflow redesign for one process usually runs eight to twelve weeks. Broader programmes covering several processes are phased over several quarters, with each phase delivering working controls.

Bring us one financial crime workflow.

We will map it, identify the control gaps and show you what a controlled redesign would involve.
